implemented_requirements.evidence: The provided snippet of `index.html` only contains a comment and the opening of the HTML document; no markup for a grid or word list is visible.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Allow the player to select four words at a time to form a group
implemented_requirements.evidence: No JavaScript or UI elements related to selection, click handling, or grouping are present in the shown portion of the file.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Validate groups, remove correct groups, and reveal a category with a color‑coded difficulty (yellow, green, blue, purple)
implemented_requirements.evidence: No code for validation, removal, category display, or difficulty colour coding is evident.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Track mistakes with a maximum of four allowed
implemented_requirements.evidence: No counter or logic for mistake tracking appears in the excerpt.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ensure only one correct solution exists (even if words seem ambiguous)
implemented_requirements.evidence: No data structures or algorithmic checks that enforce a unique solution are visible.
No shuffle function or randomisation logic is present in the provided code.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Provide immediate feedback after each guess
implemented_requirements.evidence: No UI update or feedback mechanism can be identified.
There is no evidence of date‑based seeding, server‑side generation, or any daily‑puzzle logic.

critical_issues: The supplied files contain only a comment and the start of an HTML document; the core game implementation (HTML markup, CSS, JavaScript) is missing.
No evidence of the required game mechanics (grid, selection, validation, mistake counting, colour‑coded categories) is present.
Without the functional code, the project cannot be executed or tested.
judge.summary: The submitted material does not provide any of the essential code required to realize the described puzzle game. Critical components such as the 4x4 word grid, selection handling, validation logic, mistake tracking, shuffle functionality, immediate feedback, and daily puzzle generation are absent from the evidence. Consequently, the submission fails to meet the benchmark requirements.
